h1:
The Best Hua Hin Restaurants
Great Atmosphere for a Special Meal
intro: Hua Hin has no shortage of restaurants with a great atmosphere — from beachfront seafood spots where you eat to the sound of the waves, to rooftops with 360-degree views, to dining rooms set in old houses right by the sea. These are the 11 places people talk about most, the ones that work well for a special meal, with the area, opening hours, and rough prices based on real reviews.

blocks.html: If you're in Hua Hin and want somewhere for a special meal — a birthday, an anniversary, or just bringing the family together — the town gives you plenty to choose from, from budget-friendly seafood spots right on the sand to hotel dining rooms with beautifully plated food. We picked 11 places with consistently good reviews, grouped by atmosphere to make choosing easier, and we'll tell you straight who each one suits.

items.name: Supatra by the Sea
items.blurb: A Lanna-style garden restaurant by the sea near Khao Takiab, shaded with wood and big trees, looking out over Khao Takiab hill and the water. The food is bold, flavour-forward Thai seafood, and it's a popular spot to book an evening table for the breeze and the sunset.

items.name: Baan Itsara
items.blurb: Set in a beachfront holiday house that's been open for over 25 years on Naebkehas Road, with a relaxed feel and a sea breeze. The dish people order most is clams stir-fried in basil sauce served sizzling, alongside grilled prawns. The cooking is consistent, and it suits an easygoing meal that isn't too formal.

items.name: Sang Thai Seafood
items.blurb: A long-running seafood restaurant on a wide seafront terrace near the fishing pier. Plenty of reviews praise the quality of the seafood and the brisk service. It isn't cheap, but the ingredients are fresh, and it suits anyone who wants serious seafood in Hua Hin's classic setting.

items.name: Baan Dum Oceanfront Seafood
items.blurb: Set in an old Thai-style house right at the water's edge, serving Thai seafood in a quiet, calm atmosphere where you eat to the sound of the waves. Many people pick it for a celebration without the noise, and it works well for couples or a private dinner.

items.name: Chao Lay Seafood
items.blurb: A popular seafood restaurant on a wooden deck that juts out over the sea in the centre of town. Tourists have known it for years, and it gets busy in the evening — come early or book ahead. The standout dishes are fresh grilled fish and prawns.

blocks.title: Booking tip
blocks.html: At the beachfront spots with the best views, the front-row tables fill up fast on weekend evenings. If you want a table right by the water at sunset, call ahead and ask specifically for a waterside table. Sunset in Hua Hin is around 18:00–18:45.

items.name: Vana Nava Sky Restaurant & Bar
items.blurb: A restaurant and bar on the 27th floor of the Holiday Inn Vana Nava, with near-wraparound views of the town, the mountains, and the coastline. The atmosphere is modern and upscale, the cocktails are a highlight, and it's a great spot to arrive before sunset. We'll be honest — prices run above the Hua Hin average and reviews on the food are mixed, but plenty of people feel the view makes it worth it.

items.name: Coast Beach Club & Bistro
items.blurb: An international-style beach club on Damnoen Kasem beach, with an airy, resort feel. By day you lounge on the sand; at night it turns into a bar. The international à la carte menu starts around ฿140++, and it suits an easygoing meal when you want a good atmosphere in town.

blocks.text: Hotel dining rooms and Western spots

items.name: Let's Sea Hua Hin's Beach Restaurant
items.blurb: The beachfront dining room at the Let's Sea resort, with beautifully plated food and a great setting. The dishes people talk about are the truffle-cream spaghetti and the fresh seafood. Expect around ฿501–1,000 per person — it suits a romantic dinner or a celebration.

items.name: Baan Thalia (Anantara Hua Hin)
items.blurb: The Italian restaurant at the Anantara resort, with an upscale, quiet atmosphere serving contemporary Italian food. People like to order the fresh lobster and the ravioli. It suits an important meal when you want both privacy and polished service.

items.name: Brasserie de Paris
items.blurb: A French restaurant on the seafront in the centre of town, with classics like lobster soup, foie-gras-stuffed chicken, and sole. Main dishes run around ฿150–600. It's a good choice if you want a break from Thai seafood and fancy French food in a waterside setting.

items.name: Chom Talay
items.blurb: A seafront restaurant that plenty of reviews praise for its decor and views, with an open, breezy setting and a full view of the sea. It serves Thai food and seafood, and it suits a breezy lunch or a light dinner before a stroll along the beach.

blocks.text: Pick the right place for the occasion

items: Romantic dinner for two — Let's Sea, Baan Dum, or Baan Thalia, all quiet with beautifully plated food
Family seafood celebration — Sang Thai, Supatra by the Sea, or Chao Lay, where it's fun to order and share
Want a view for photos — Vana Nava Sky at sunset, or Coast Beach Club on the sand
A change to Western food — Brasserie de Paris (French) or Baan Thalia (Italian)

blocks.title: About the cost
blocks.html: The prices on this page are rough figures from reviews and can change with the menu and the season. Resort and rooftop restaurants often add a service charge and tax. If you're on a tight budget, it's worth checking the menu or calling ahead.

faq.q: Which Hua Hin restaurants have a great atmosphere for a special meal?
faq.a: For a romantic special meal, Let's Sea, Baan Dum, and Baan Thalia at the Anantara are all great for atmosphere and beautifully plated food. If you want a wide view, Vana Nava Sky on the 27th floor is a popular choice.

faq.q: Which beachfront restaurants in Hua Hin do people talk about most?
faq.a: Supatra by the Sea near Khao Takiab, Baan Itsara on Naebkehas Road, Sang Thai Seafood near the fishing pier, and Chao Lay in town are all beachfront spots with consistently good reviews.

faq.q: Do I need to book a table ahead?
faq.a: On weekends and Friday-to-Sunday evenings, the beachfront spots with the best views get very busy. It's worth calling to book and asking for a waterside table, especially if you want one for the sunset around 18:00–18:45.

Beachfront seafood spots generally run a few hundred baht per person depending on what you order. Resort dining rooms like Let's Sea are around ฿501–1,000 per person, and rooftops like Vana Nava Sky run above the town average. Budget for service charge and tax too.

faq.q: What Western restaurants in Hua Hin are worth trying?
faq.a: Brasserie de Paris serves French food on the seafront, with mains around ฿150–600. Baan Thalia at the Anantara serves contemporary Italian in an upscale setting — both are good if you want a break from Thai seafood.
